name: Hillary Clinton
role: US First Lady (1993–2001), Senator from New York (2001–2009), Secretary of State (2009–2013) and 2016 Democratic presidential nominee
summary: Hillary Clinton is a mainstream American Democrat who calls herself a progressive who gets things done. She favours higher taxes on the wealthy, expanded health coverage built on the ACA, tighter financial rules, labor rights and civil rights for women and LGBT people, with a strong commitment to US alliances and a record of backing military force in Iraq, Libya and Syria.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Defends and would expand the ACA, would build toward a public option, and says she has never given up on universal coverage; in 2016 she called Medicare-for-all not feasible, so the goal is long term and not a single government plan.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Proposed a $12 federal minimum wage, said she would sign $15 if Congress passed it, and in the 2016 debates called for raising the national minimum wage and ending the tipped wage.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Platform imposes a surcharge on multi-millionaires and billionaires, backs the Buffett Rule and closes carried interest; debates: the wealthy and corporations should pay their fair share.

unions-good.rationale: Labor platform states unions helped build the middle class and remain essential; she co-sponsored the Employee Free Choice Act.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Platform adds a risk fee on large financial firms, closes the Volcker loophole, gives regulators power to break up risky firms, and defends Dodd-Frank; the tighter rules are aimed mainly at finance and offshoring.

cut-welfare.rationale: Her 2016 anti-poverty platform expands the child tax credit and rental assistance. She called the 1990s welfare reform a critical step despite flaws, so the evidence leans against cutting.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Platform proposes an intelligence surge and monitoring of ISIS communications and social media to stop attacks; she voted for the Patriot Act in 2001 and its 2006 renewal after pressing civil-liberty fixes.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Platform seeks rescheduling marijuana to Schedule II and lets states experiment; reporting in 2014 shows she took a wait-and-see view of recreational legalization. No call to legalise recreational drugs.

limit-guns.rationale: Backs universal background checks, closing gun-show and online loopholes, keeping military-style weapons off the street and ending industry immunity, while saying she supports an individual Second Amendment right.

empower-police-military.rationale: Mixed record: platform stresses police accountability (body cameras, use-of-force guidelines, ending profiling) while she co-introduced a bill adding 80,000 Army soldiers in 2005 and called for ending the defense sequester.

rehabilitation.rationale: Platform puts treatment over incarceration for low-level nonviolent drug offenders, funds $5 billion for re-entry jobs and calls to end the era of mass incarceration.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In March 2013 she said she supports marriage for lesbian and gay couples personally and as a matter of policy and law (earlier in 2008 she favoured civil unions); the 2016 platform welcomes the Supreme Court ruling.

abortion-legal.rationale: Says she strongly supports Roe v. Wade and safe and legal abortion; platform defends Planned Parenthood and access to care.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Platform has a barriers-to-opportunity agenda with $125 billion in targeted investment and criminal justice reform aimed at racial disparities; in the 2016 debate she called for addressing systemic racism in criminal justice.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Platform seeks comprehensive reform with a path to citizenship, clearing the family visa backlog and naturalisation help, and in 2015 she backed accepting 65,000 Syrian refugees; she also stresses secure borders.

free-trade.rationale: Mixed: she voted against CAFTA, opposed the final TPP and called for tougher enforcement and a trade prosecutor, yet said the US must trade with the other 95 percent of the world and backed other trade deals.

nation-first.rationale: Argues US alliances have kept the peace and that without US leadership there is a vacuum; calls NATO one of the best investments America has made.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: As Secretary of State she backed the 2011 Libya intervention, saying it prevented a massacre, and in 2015 supported a Syrian no-fly zone; later called it too soon to judge Libya.

open-borders.rationale: Stated in the 2016 debate that there will not be open borders and pledged secure borders, explaining her earlier common-market remark was about energy grids.

limit-growth.rationale: Frames climate action as an opportunity to grow the economy and calls for a full-employment economy with shared growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Platform sets 80 percent emissions cuts by 2050, defends and extends the Clean Power Plan, a $60 billion clean energy challenge and half a billion solar panels in her first term.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Reported as supporting keeping safe existing plants open and investing in advanced nuclear, and saying nuclear power is needed for the climate challenge (October 2016); in 2007 she called herself agnostic.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Tax platform says very large multi-million-dollar estates should pay their share.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Platform calls for large public investment in infrastructure, manufacturing, clean energy and research, with a $10 billion Make it in America plan; it does not frame this as directing capital to named strategic industries.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Pledges to pay for her priorities without adding to the national debt and called Bush tax cuts fiscally irresponsible, though her platform includes large infrastructure spending.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Called the 1996 welfare reform a critical step despite flaws and backed moving able recipients from welfare into jobs.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Geneva speech: all persons are free and equal in dignity and rights and are equally entitled to human rights; Beijing speech makes the same claim for women.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Geneva speech condemns criminalising homosexuality and argues violence and discrimination against gay people violate human rights; she says gay rights are human rights.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Says US alliances have kept the peace, defends NATO Article 5 and commits to strengthening partnerships.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Supports NATO and describes it as one of the best investments America has made; the 2016 debate stresses alliances.

collective-defense.rationale: Explained NATO Article 5 in the 2016 debate as an attack on one is an attack on all and praised NATO invoking it after 9/11.

death-penalty.rationale: Said she does not favour abolishing the death penalty because of certain egregious cases, limited to federal cases like terrorism and mass killings (Oklahoma City, 9/11), while saying it has been applied unfairly by states.

school-vouchers.rationale: Reported as opposing school vouchers while supporting charter schools and public school choice.

corporate-influence.rationale: Platform says the political system has been hijacked by billionaires and special interests; she would overturn Citizens United by amendment and require disclosure of political spending.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Voted against CAFTA in 2005 citing weak labor and environmental standards and called for renegotiating NAFTA standards.

no-bailouts.rationale: Voted for TARP in October 2008, a vote in favour of public money for failing banks, though her platform aims to end too-big-to-fail.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: At the December 2015 debate she called for government and tech companies to work together so law enforcement can access encrypted terrorist communications, while saying she would not want to mandate backdoors.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Platform backs easier gender-marker changes on documents, protection from violence, the Equality Act and she updated passport policy as Secretary of State.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Platform applauds the Pentagon letting transgender personnel serve openly and would upgrade records of LGBT veterans discharged for orientation.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Platform commits to work for the Equality Act and court efforts barring discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity in public life.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Platform proposes reforming police (body cameras, training, use-of-force guidelines) and prisons rather than abolishing them.

abolish-ip.rationale: Platform would improve the patent system to reward innovators and protect copyright, opposing piracy of US intellectual property.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Platform supports the PACT Act, stricter puppy-mill rules, ending horse slaughter and humane treatment of farm animals; she earned a perfect Humane Society score as senator.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Platform encourages farms to raise animals humanely and cut non-therapeutic antibiotics without calling for an end to animal farming; no stated position on research.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Platform lets borrowers refinance, caps repayments at 10 percent of income with forgiveness after 20 years, and offers up to $17,500 forgiveness for social entrepreneurs.

free-public-college.rationale: Platform makes community college tuition-free and in-state public four-year tuition free for families earning up to $125,000 (phased in), not for all students.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: In the 2016 debate she said race remains a significant challenge and called for addressing systemic racism in the criminal justice system.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Voted for the 2002 Iraq authorisation (later called it a mistake), backed the Libya intervention and a Syria no-fly zone, so she has not limited force to defence.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Said she favoured arming Syrian rebels with regional partners and supporting Kurdish forces against Assad.

arms-reduction.rationale: Helped complete the New START treaty as Secretary of State, which cut US and Russian arsenals, and stresses reducing nuclear proliferation.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Describes herself as an unwavering supporter of Israel, backs a two-state solution and supports its security and qualitative military edge.

social-market-economy.rationale: Favors inclusive capitalism: markets paired with worker profit-sharing, financial rules and social programs.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Platform pledges to restore collective bargaining rights, and she co-sponsored the Employee Free Choice Act.

paid-care-work.rationale: Platform gives Social Security credit for years out of work as a caregiver, tax relief for caregivers and paid family leave; it does not call to pay domestic work as labour.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Platform says the political system is hijacked by billionaires and special interests.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Platform backs an open internet abroad and the free flow of information across borders; reports show she criticised Chinese internet monitoring.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Platform would cut oil and gas tax subsidies, reform federal leasing and expand clean energy on public lands tenfold, with fossil production safe and responsible; she opposed Arctic drilling.

taxation-theft.rationale: Her platform proposes higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations to fund public investment, which treats taxation as legitimate.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Platform backs the Buffett Rule and a surcharge on multi-millionaires, a rising rate structure rather than a flat one.

state-harmful.rationale: Platform relies on large public programs and investment (infrastructure, health, education), the opposite of the claim the state is unnecessary and harmful.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Platform expands government roles in health coverage, education, labor and infrastructure well beyond defence, justice and property.

notes: Same-sex marriage: favoured civil unions in 2008, then announced support for marriage in March 2013 (most recent used). TPP: praised it as Secretary of State, opposed the final deal from 2015 (opposition used). Iraq: voted for the 2002 authorisation and later called it a mistake; the later view is reflected in the Iraq-related answers. Bill Clinton's positions were not used. Wayback Machine access was blocked in this environment, so the 2016 campaign issue pages were read from hillaryclinton.com directly; her books were not available as full text and were not used.
